newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MMS postpones meetings on oil valuation plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MMS postpones meetings on oil valuation plan.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service said Thursday it would postpone two public meetings to discuss its proposal to change the way it assesses royalties owed on oil production from leases on federal land.
The first meeting, originally set for February 25, will now be held March 27 in Houston, Texas.
The second meeting, originally set for March 4, will be held April 3 in Lakewood, Colorado, MMS said.
The meetings were rescheduled to give industry more time to prepare comments on the controversial proposal.

In a bid to ensure that oil companies were not cheating the government of royalties, MMS last month proposed to base royalty calculations on crude oil futures prices instead of on company posted prices, saying that posted prices did not reflect the market value of the oil.
